import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import math

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, (nn.Conv2d, nn.Linear)):
                nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=math.sqrt(2.0))
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
        nn.init.orthogonal_(self.place_head.weight, gain=0.01)
        nn.init.orthogonal_(self.done_head.weight, gain=0.01)
        nn.init.orthogonal_(self.value_head.weight, gain=1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
DEPTH = 3
HID = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * WIDTH, HID, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps
        ])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        outs = []
        for fp, head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            dy, dx = fp
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 36
NBLOCKS = 3
CW = 16


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1) for _ in range(NBLOCKS)])
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, CW, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(CW, CW, 3, padding=1)
        self.cglob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * CW, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        for conv in self.blocks:
            f = f + F.relu(conv(f))
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        c = F.relu(self.c1(obs))
        c = c + F.relu(self.c2(c))
        cg = self.cglob(torch.cat([c.mean((2, 3)), c.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        return logits, self.value_head(cg).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting network's 4 seeds scored 0.068, 0.068, 0.068 and 0.258, so outcomes split into two groups: most runs stall at the same 0.068 level and a few break out. Two lessons follow. First, the budget is about 32 PPO updates, and any extra compute cuts samples in proportion, so candidates should stay close to the starting network's compute (r ≈ 1). Second, better reliability across seeds may matter as much as more capacity. The agent has to judge, for each anchor, whether the brick lands exactly on the target layer across its whole footprint. That is the highest build cell under several cells, so it is a local max over the footprint, and the network should learn it from local features. DONE needs a global check that no target cells are still missing. This round tests three things: training stability through initialisation, a wider view through depth at the same compute, and a placement head that pools learned features over each brick's footprint.
analyses.2: The residual body (r1c2: a stem plus 3 residual 3x3 blocks, width 40) scored 0.40. Both of its seeds (0.49 and 0.31) are above every baseline seed, which ranged from 0.068 to 0.258. That is strong evidence that more depth and a wider view help, not just luck. The footprint-pooled head on a plain 3-layer body scored 0.27. That is above the baseline, but its body had no residual links, so the head's own effect is mixed up with the extra depth. Orthogonal init (0.15) is within noise of the baseline, so init is not the main limit. Next tests: (1) push depth further at about the same compute (6 blocks, width 32, so the view covers the whole 10x10 grid); (2) put the footprint head on top of the residual body; (3) a new idea: KataGo-style global pooling biases in each block. These let each cell use board-wide state (what is finished, which layers are next) to decide placement order.
analyses.3: The residual body is the one clear win: r1c2 (3 blocks, width 40) scored 0.401, against 0.116 for the starting network over 4 seeds. Its add-ons, the footprint head (0.305) and the global pooling bias (0.341), are within seed noise of it and add compute without a clear gain. Six blocks at width 32 dropped to 0.155, with one seed collapsing. That run changed depth and width together, and residual sums with no normalisation only grow, so the cause is unclear. Seed luck remains large: the gap between r1c2's two seeds alone is 0.19. Training takes about 55 of the 900 seconds allowed, so time is not limiting. Since there is little evidence for extra modules, I keep r1c2 and test three single changes: a near-uniform starting policy (to cut seed failures), dilated convolutions (whole-grid view at the same compute and depth) and width 48 (capacity against fewer samples).
analyses.4: r1c2 (3 residual blocks, width 40, r≈1.05) is still clearly the best at 0.40. The strongest pattern: every candidate with r of 1.2 or more scored lower, because higher r means fewer samples. Those were width 48 (0.05), 6 blocks (0.16), footprint heads (0.27 and 0.30). Dilation hurt (0.13), so local detail matters more than seeing the whole grid. Small-gain heads (0.29) and global pooling (0.34) gave no gain. Global pooling did have the steadiest seeds. This is the last round and the top 3 go to 4-seed evaluation. So I test small changes near r1c2 that keep r at or below 1: a narrower body for the full 131k steps; that body with a separate critic, so value loss stops disturbing the shared trunk; and one more block at the same compute.
